newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two in race for deputy governor at Banco de Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Two in race for deputy governor at Banco de Mexico.

text.p: Two high-level government officials are in the running to replace the outgoing deputy governor, Ariel Buira, at Banco de Mexico, analysts said on Thursday.
They add that the new deputy governor, one of four at the central bank, is likely to be a central bank insider.
"This is an insider whose term expires, and my guess is that they will pick an insider to take his place," said Mexico City economist Jonathan Heath.
The two names that top the list of rumoured replacements are both central bank veterans: deputy finance minister Jose Sidaoui, and central bank director of Economic Analysis Agustin Carstens.

"Sidaoui is somebody who has has always been in the Banco of Mexico and he is on loan there (at Finance) to be the undersecretary. But before that you could say that the two top people below the board of governors were Sidaoui and Carstens and obviously you could say that these are the first two names that come up," said Heath.
Analysts speculate that the decision has already been made and will be announced when the central bank unveils its 1997 monetary policy program within the next few days.
"The name we hear the most strongly is Carstens," said one Mexico City economist who declined to be identified.

Analysts say that whoever replaces Buira, policy at the central bank will remain unchanged. Central bank governor Miguel Mancera reiterated on the weekend that the central bank would continue to do its best to reduce inflation.
There has been some speculation that the new deputy governor would be a favorite to replace governor Mancera, who is due to retire next year.
But central bank watchers say that deputy governor Francisco Gil Diaz is the most probable candidate to replace Mancera.
"Right now the most likely candidate is Gil Diaz. Whoever is the second person on that list is well below the first person," Heath said.
Buira's term expires on December 31 this year, and his replacement is expected to be be ratified by Congress before year's end.

Mexico City newspaper El Financiero also speculated recently that Federal Competition Comission chief Pascual Garcia de Alba, and the president of the National Banking Commission, Eduardo Fernandez, were in the running to replace Buira.
